description: An astrocyte is a large, star-shaped type of glial cell found exclusively in the central nervous system (the brain and spinal cord).
summary:
We developed an AI-powered health monitoring system for astronauts on long missions. The algorithm evaluates 43 physiological variables and 12 risks associated with the space environment according to NASA's Human Research Program and translates them into color-coded risk banding, seven-day forecast, and specific countermeasures. Rather than framing space adaptation as a disease, the proposed algorithm disassociates health from the space environment and quantifies the amount of additional risk imposed specifically by the space environment. A safety floor guarantees that the AI will never downplay any critical alerts (red or black) in the reference range.

Our solution tackles the challenge by enabling astronauts to evaluate their own health state using manual input, wearables, ECG, and voice data. It introduces explanations for non-doctor users, gamification of tasks, food intake logging, and six mission profiles, from International Space Station to Mars. The system continues to function even during communication blackout periods with Earth.

This is important since for a Mars mission, the one-way time delay is around 12.5 minutes and evacuation lasts about 180 days. Therefore, crews need to be able to identify the emerging issues at an early stage and manage them independently.
details:
We as the team of AstrocyteX have programmed our project, AstroGuard-X, a medical telemetry and clinical support control engineered for space missions (Lunar Gateway, Artemis surface habitats, ISS environment, deep space and Mars transit). The health parameters/data are provided to the system and analysed. A risk assesment is made for each parametere. The data streams consist of: 31 physiological, biochemical and clinical markers which include ongoing, wearable streams gathering information about such vitality parameters as heart rate, SpO2, systolic and diastolic BP, respiratory rate, core temperature, galvanic skin response, sleep pattern, hydration and fluid balance, urine and saliva testing strips, ARED resistance exercises and treadmill loads, blood analysis at the point of service, CBC, and nutrition.

12 NASA RIDGE channels of spaceflight hazards such as radiation dose and solar flares, isolation and confinement periods, latency in communication with the Earth, gravity field (zero gravity, Moon gravity 0.16g, Mars gravity 0.38g or hyper-G) and the confined environment that can relate to living (ppO2, CO2 mmHg, NH3, cabin pressure, noise level, temperature and humidity and microbial richness of water).

Electrocardiographic monitor measures the 10 rhythm and conduction parameters defining normal rhythm, atrial fibrillation, atrial flutter, left and right bundle branch blocks, myocardial infarction, PVCs, PACs and AVB, also registering QTc, PR, QRS intervals and ST segment and making STEMI changes and synchronizing cardiac risk with the central system of telemetric combination.

Astronaut Voice Acoustics & Psychological Biomarkers (AstroVoiceNet v1.0): Analyzes live 16 kHz microphone recordings or uploaded audio clips based on 48-band log-Mel spectrograms and 42 GeMAPS inspired prosodic features (F0, jitter, shimmer, HNR, formants, pause dynamics) to detect 5 respiratory states (Calm/regulated, Cognitive Fatigue, Acute Stress, Low Mood/Isolation, Dyspnea/Hypoxic Strain) and 4 continuous affect dimensions (valence, arousal, stress, fatigue).

Longitudinal Health. AI advisor (LLM) records time-stamped crew snapshots into a -column telemetry comparison matrix and comparative bar chart while a role-adaptive advisor switches seamlessly between "I am a doctor" (quantitative aerospace pathophysiology for flight surgeons) and "I am not a doctor" (calm jargon-free support, for crew).

Every neural inference model (AstrocyteXNet v3.0, AstroVoiceNet v1.0 12-lead ECG screening and a deterministic aerospace-medicine edge reasoner) runs locally on CPU or GPU with millisecond latency—requiring zero cloud connectivity when Earth links drop while optionally connecting to Google Gemini 2.5 Flash when ground bandwidth is available. Shifts that look pathological on Earth distinguished from genuine emergencies. Crew stress, isolation-induced low mood, cognitive fatigue and cabin hypoxia are detected passively from a seconds of natural speech without invasive hardware.

The backbone of the neural structure has the following components: A Mamba-2 Structured State Space Duality (SSD) encoder, Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT), Feature-wise Linear Modulation (FiLM), 16-latent Preciver Cross Attention, Physics Informed Neural ODE/PINN and Bayesian/Monte Carlo Droupout Residual Risk Calculator. It contains around 2.98 million parameters.

An integrated operational protocol engine converts elevated risk bands into countermeasure tasks and reinforces long-duration compliance through XP, rank progression, daily streaks and operational badges.

The project is aimed to provide astronouts with specific health tasks involved with their health status. It is also aimed to be an assistance tools for medical personels and emergency situation help. Especially in case of the communication between the crew and the Earth is cut, it may come in handy in terms of health monitoring. It empowers non-physician astronauts and remote patients to act confidently during medical anomalies.

Programming Languages used are Python 3.10–3.13 (AI models, physics-informed simulation, REST backend, automated testing) and Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5 Canvas, Web Audio API, and CSS3 (zero-build dark-space telemetry SPA).

Tools used for deep learning and scientific track are PyTorch 2.8 (CUDA 12.6 & CPU portable execution), NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, scikit-learn, Matplotlib, and custom implementations of Mamba-2 SSD, Temporal Fusion Transformer, Perceiver Cross-Attention, FiLM, Neural ODE / PINN, Bayes-by-Backprop, Depthwise-Separable Squeeze-and-Excitation CNNs, and GeMAPS

Tools used for backend, storage and dual UI are FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic v2, SQLite (persistent longitudinal crew snapshots, countermeasures, and telemetry history), custom Vanilla JS Web Console, secondary Streamlit dashboard, and google genaiintegration.

Developed and trained on a Windows workstation equipped with an NVIDIA CUDA-enabled laptop GPU and standard 16 kHz microphone input engineered to run on standard CPU-only laptops without external hardware.

Our project is creative for many reasons. Firstly, it uses a very creative neural backbone. Especially the usage of the Neural ODE (PINN) helps the modeling of microgravity fluid shift, plasma volume loss, bone demineralization and muscle atrophy. Usage of Temporal Convolutional Network and Temporal Fusion Transformer strenghens feature extraction and helps handling multi horizon forecasting.

Combining vocal biomarkers from AstroVoiceNet with 12-lead ECG morphology and 43 biochemical and environmental channels creates a complete digital twin of the crew’s mind and body. Dual-Persona Medical Communication allows a single toggle to switch between two modes: one for doctors and one for non-doctors. In the doctor mode the system delivers summaries and interactive Q&A that include quantitative pathophysiology data like F0, QTc and counterfactual risk uplift. In the -doctor mode the same system gives clear reassuring step-, by-step instructions to astronauts. Our project also contains gamification, through which specific tasks are provided to the astronaut and by fulfilling them they get badges and points which motivates them to fulfill the tasks. It also contains a health tracker, which tracks the health status of the astronaut over time. The integration of specific missions such as Lunar mission, ISS and Mars environment-adapted system which allows for the setting of the values of the parameters in the essence of the mission selected. That a UI is designed in the first place makes the interraction with the system simple to understand. Its also offline and does not need internet.

Our team considered many factors through brainstorming, some of which impacted the creation of the neural network. The health parameters that would be added to the system were firstly discussed and researched through NASA’s own sources (for example NASA STD-3001) and many other academic research papers. We also searched about the formulation of the neural network and discussed with each other and decided on the current version.
